feed.title: Amplify: what's new
feed.subtitle: Youth voice news and Amplify releases. Generated from data/latest.json and data/changelog.json.

entry.title: UK Parliament Week, 23 to 29 November 2026
entry.summary: Parliament's annual week of democracy activity, with free kits for schools, youth groups and adults. Amplify plans to launch on its first day. Source: UK Parliament Education.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0: Launch at UK Parliament Week 2026
entry.summary: Public launch planned for the first day of UK Parliament Week (23 to 29 November 2026), subject to the owner's decision to share it.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.7: Measure without tracking
entry.summary: The graphics pack is also published as a GitHub release file so its total downloads can be counted with no tracking on the portal, and the contact form now tells anyone worried about their safety where to go instead.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.6: Every way to take part
entry.summary: A new Foundations screen on young people's political and civic participation, by age and nation, every fact sourced, with a register of participation gaps; eight new glossary terms.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.5: Inside Parliament
entry.summary: A new Foundations screen on how Parliament actually runs, in six tabs, with every fact sourced and dated, and eight new glossary terms.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.4: Weekly upkeep: helplines re-checked, two new updates
entry.summary: Helplines re-verified against each service's own website on 16 November 2026; no closures or number changes. Two dated, sourced updates added to What's new, and two new glossary terms.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.3: Campaign kit redesign for UK Parliament Week
entry.summary: The campaign collateral redesigned from a scan of award-winning youth campaigns, inside the Brand & style rules, with a downloadable graphics pack (defects D30 to D34).

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.2: Safeguarding and honesty fixes before launch
entry.summary: Four launch blockers fixed (defects D25 to D28), and the readiness record brought up to date.

entry.title: Amplify 1.0.0-rc.1: Sources, safeguards, self-checks and help
entry.summary: Everything below is new or changed since the first published build earlier today.

entry.title: Amplify 0.1.0: First published build
entry.summary: The Claude Design project turned into a page that can be sent: portal view first, unofficial-prototype notices, the footer and colophon, and fonts and scripts served by the portal itself.

entry.title: MPs debate the review of young people and work
entry.summary: A review of young people and work commissioned by the Work and Pensions Secretary (the Milburn review) published its interim report in May 2026: nearly one million 16 to 24 year olds in the UK are NEET, 957,000 at the end of 2025. MPs debated it in Westminster Hall on 3 November 2026. The final report is due later in 2026. Source: Young People and Work interim report (GOV.UK); Hansard.

entry.title: Votes at 16 Bill reaches Lords committee stage
entry.summary: The House of Lords began its Committee of the Whole House on the Representation of the People Bill on 2 November 2026, with a second day on 4 November and six days provisionally allocated. Peers can now propose changes line by line. It is not yet law. Source: Hansard Society, Parliament Matters Bulletin; confirm each stage on Parliament's bill page.

entry.title: April 2027 minimum wage rates announced
entry.summary: The Government accepted the Low Pay Commission's advice in full: £13.21 for 21 and over and £11.27 for 18 to 20, from 1 April 2027. Until then the April 2026 rates apply. Source: GOV.UK, Low Pay Commission.

entry.title: HOPELINE247 has closed
entry.summary: PAPYRUS Prevention of Young Suicide entered administration on 7 September 2026 and its HOPELINE247 helpline is no longer operating. The administrators point people to Samaritans (116 123), Shout (text SHOUT to 85258), NHS 111, or 999 in an emergency. This portal has removed HOPELINE247 from its helplines. Source: Joint Administrators, Opus Restructuring.

entry.title: Votes at 16 Bill clears the Commons
entry.summary: The Representation of the People Bill completed its Commons third reading on 2 September 2026 and moved to the House of Lords. It is not yet law. Source: Reported by MPs and bill trackers; confirm each stage on Parliament's bill page.

entry.title: 981,000 young people not earning or learning
entry.summary: Official estimates show around 981,000 16 to 24 year olds were NEET in April to June 2026, down from 1,012,000 in January to March, the highest since 2013. Source: Office for National Statistics, via Youth Futures Foundation.

entry.title: Sign Language Act (Northern Ireland) becomes law
entry.summary: Northern Ireland's Sign Language Act received Royal Assent on 9 July 2026, recognising both British Sign Language and Irish Sign Language and placing duties on public bodies to make information and services accessible. Source: Department for Communities (Northern Ireland).

entry.title: Social media ban for under 16s announced
entry.summary: The Government announced that major social media platforms will be barred from serving under 16s, with livestreaming banned for under 16s and stranger contact blocked by default for under 17s. Regulations are due before Christmas 2026, to apply from spring 2027. Campaigners under 16 should plan to work through MYPs, school councils and adult allies rather than personal accounts. Source: UK Government announcement, widely reported (Reuters, BBC).

entry.title: New minimum wage rates in force
entry.summary: £12.71 for 21 and over, £10.85 for 18 to 20, and £8 for under 18s and apprentices, from 1 April 2026. The 18 to 20 rate rose 8.5%. Source: GOV.UK.

entry.title: Youth Select Committee reports on PSHE
entry.summary: The Youth Select Committee called on the UK Government to end the postcode lottery in PSHE teaching. Source: National Youth Agency.

entry.title: Representation of the People Bill introduced
entry.summary: The Government introduced the Bill that would extend the vote to 16 and 17 year olds in all UK elections. Source: GOV.UK.

entry.title: National Youth Strategy published
entry.summary: Youth Matters, a ten-year strategy for 10 to 21 year olds in England (up to 25 with SEND), backed by over £500 million and shaped by over 14,000 young people. Source: Department for Culture, Media and Sport.

entry.title: UK Youth Parliament sits in the Commons
entry.summary: Members of Youth Parliament debated the 2025 manifesto priorities in the House of Commons Chamber in November 2025, chaired by the Speaker. Source: Scottish Youth Parliament and local councils' reports.

entry.title: National Citizen Service closed
entry.summary: NCS programme delivery ended on 31 March 2025 and the NCS Trust closed on 11 July 2025. Source: GOV.UK.
